title: Simultaneous compactification of a proper correspondence diagram
statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X,Y,C,B$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $c_i:C\to X$, $b_i:B\to Y$ ($i=1,2$) be $k$-morphisms, and let $p:X\to Y$, $q:C\to B$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $b_iq=pc_i$. There exist proper finite-type $k$-schemes $X^*,Y^*,C^*,B^*$, dense open immersions $u_X:X\hookrightarrow X^*$, $u_Y:Y\hookrightarrow Y^*$, $u_C:C\hookrightarrow C^*$, $u_B:B\hookrightarrow B^*$ [def-weil-open-immersion], proper maps $p^*:X^*\to Y^*$, $q^*:C^*\to B^*$, and maps $c_i^*:C^*\to X^*$, $b_i^*:B^*\to Y^*$ such that
$$p^*u_X=u_Yp,\quad q^*u_C=u_Bq,\quad c_i^*u_C=u_Xc_i,\quad b_i^*u_B=u_Yb_i,\quad b_i^*q^*=p^*c_i^*.$$
Here dense means topologically dense. Moreover the squares $(u_X,p,u_Y,p^*)$ and $(u_C,q,u_B,q^*)$ are Cartesian: the natural maps $X\to X^*\times_{Y^*}Y$ and $C\to C^*\times_{B^*}B$ are isomorphisms. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed on the original leg squares, and no original scheme is required to be proper over $k$.

source.place: §4.1.4(a), final paragraph, using the graph-closure construction of Remark 1.1.3; Cartesian restriction squares follow from properness and density

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. Since $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and each of $X,Y,C,B$ is separated and of finite type over $S$, [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] gives dense compactifications. Choose first a proper compactification $u_Y:Y\hookrightarrow Y^*$ of $Y$, and choose auxiliary compactifications $j_B:B\hookrightarrow B'$, $j_X:X\hookrightarrow X'$, and $j_C:C\hookrightarrow C'$; these auxiliary schemes will only supply the first factors of the later scheme-theoretic closures. All four auxiliary compactifications are proper and finite type over $S$.

source.place: Remark 1.1.3 and §4.1.4(a), final paragraph: choose compactifications before taking closures

proof.text: Define the tuple map $h_B=(j_B,u_Yb_1,u_Yb_2):B\to B'\times_S Y^*\times_S Y^*$. It is quasi-compact because $B$ is Noetherian. It is an immersion: it is the composite of the graph $\Gamma=(\mathrm{id}_B,u_Yb_1,u_Yb_2):B\to B\times_S Y^*\times_S Y^*$, a section of the projection to $B$, which is separated as the base change of the separated $Y^*\times_SY^*\to S$, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], followed by $j_B\times\mathrm{id}$, the base change of the open immersion $j_B$, hence an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Let $B^*$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $h_B$. By [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure], the factor $u_B:B\hookrightarrow B^*$ is a dense open immersion. The two projections of the ambient product define maps $b_i^*:B^*\to Y^*$ and, by construction, $b_i^*u_B=u_Yb_i$. The product $B'\times_SY^*\times_SY^*\to S$ is proper as a composite of base changes of proper maps [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], so its closed subscheme $B^*$ is proper (hence finite type) over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c).

source.place: Remark 1.1.3: closure of the tuple $(j',j_1c_1,j_2c_2)$ and projection maps

proof.text: Define $h_X=(j_X,u_Yp):X\to T_X:=X'\times_S Y^*$ and let $X^*$ be its scheme-theoretic image. It is a quasi-compact immersion, and hence separated by the immersion clause of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation]. The closure node gives a dense open immersion $u_X:X\hookrightarrow X^*$, while projection to $Y^*$ gives $p^*:X^*\to Y^*$ and $p^*u_X=u_Yp$. We prove the Cartesian assertion over $Y$. Put $T_{X,Y}=X'\times_S Y$, an open subscheme of $T_X$, and let $h_{X,Y}=(j_X,p):X\to T_{X,Y}$. This is an immersion (the graph $(\mathrm{id}_X,p):X\to X\times_SY$ is a section of the separated projection to $X$, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], followed by $j_X\times\mathrm{id}_Y$, an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; likewise for $h_X$, quasi-compact as $X$ is Noetherian), and it is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation]. Its composite with the projection $T_{X,Y}\to Y$ is the proper map $p$. The target projection is separated and locally of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-image-proper] says that the scheme-theoretic image $Z_X$ of $h_{X,Y}$ is proper over $Y$ and that $X\to Z_X$ is surjective. The closure node says that $X\to Z_X$ is also an open immersion, hence an isomorphism; therefore $h_{X,Y}$ is a closed immersion and in particular is proper. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] to this proper immersion confirms the closed-immersion conclusion. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] to $h_X:X\to T_X$ with the open $T_{X,Y}=T_X\times_{Y^*}Y$. It identifies $X^*\times_{T_X}T_{X,Y}=X^*\times_{Y^*}Y$ with the scheme-theoretic image of $h_{X,Y}$, namely $X$, giving the required isomorphism. The projection $X^*\to Y^*$ is proper: $X'\times_SY^*\to Y^*$ is the base change of the proper $X'\to S$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and its composite with the closed immersion $X^*\to X'\times_SY^*$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](b).

source.place: §4.1.4(a), final paragraph, with the scheme-theoretic closure and open restriction supplying the Cartesian refinement

proof.text: Define $h_C=(j_C,u_Bq,u_Xc_1,u_Xc_2):C\to T_C:=C'\times_S B^*\times_S X^*\times_S X^*$ and let $C^*$ be its scheme-theoretic image. It is a quasi-compact immersion, and hence separated by the immersion clause of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation]. The closure node gives a dense open immersion $u_C:C\hookrightarrow C^*$; the projections give $q^*:C^*\to B^*$ and $c_i^*:C^*\to X^*$, with $q^*u_C=u_Bq$ and $c_i^*u_C=u_Xc_i$. To prove the Cartesian assertion over $B$, restrict to the open $T_{C,B}:=C'\times_S B\times_S X^*\times_S X^*$ and the tuple map $h_{C,B}=(j_C,q,u_Xc_1,u_Xc_2)$. It is an immersion (graph of $(q,u_Xc_1,u_Xc_2)$, a section of a separated projection [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion], followed by the open immersion $j_C\times\mathrm{id}$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; likewise for $h_C$, quasi-compact as $C$ is Noetherian) and is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation]; its composite with the projection to $B$ is the proper map $q$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-image-proper] gives a proper scheme-theoretic image over $B$ and a surjective factor from $C$, while [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] makes that factor an open immersion. Hence it is an isomorphism, so $h_{C,B}$ is a proper closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] applies as well. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] to $h_C:C\to T_C$ with the open $T_{C,B}=T_C\times_{B^*}B$. It identifies the image of $h_{C,B}$ with $C^*\times_{T_C}T_{C,B}=C^*\times_{B^*}B$, so the canonical map $C\to C^*\times_{B^*}B$ is an isomorphism. The projection $q^*$ is proper: $T_C\to B^*$ is a base change of the proper $C'\times_SX^*\times_SX^*\to S$ (proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], $X^*$ being proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c)), and composing with the closed immersion $C^*\to T_C$ keeps it proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](b).

source.place: §4.1.4(a), final paragraph, applying the same closure construction to the source correspondence

proof.text: The tuple definitions give $b_i^*u_B=u_Yb_i$, $c_i^*u_C=u_Xc_i$, and the displayed equations for $p^*$ and $q^*$. On the dense open $C$ the two maps $b_i^*q^*,p^*c_i^*:C^*\to Y^*$ agree, because $b_iq=pc_i$; since $Y^*\to S$ is separated, [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] makes them equal on all of $C^*$. The closures are proper over $S$ by Steps 2-4 and $Y^*$ by Step 1. The four open immersions are scheme-theoretically dense ([sk-thm-nagata-compactification] for $u_Y$, [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] for the others), hence topologically dense: if an open $V$ of the compactification missed the open image $U$, then $\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O_U(U\cap V)=0$ would be injective, so $\mathcal O(V)=0$ and $V=\emptyset$. The two isomorphisms just proved are exactly the Cartesian squares under [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. No Cartesian property of the original leg squares and no properness of the original schemes over $k$ was used.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned proof by following the required ordered scheme-theoretic-image route. First choose Y* and auxiliary compactifications; form B* as the closure of the tuple (j_B,u_Yb_1,u_Yb_2), then X* as the closure of (j_X,u_Yp), and finally C* as the closure of (j_C,u_Bq,u_Xc_1,u_Xc_2). The proper-image, separated-cancellation, proper-immersion, and open-restriction nodes now prove the two Cartesian inverse-image identities. The invalid independent graph closures, common-modification step, and tuple replacement were removed.
split_report.blueprint: Varshavsky Remark 1.1.3 tuple-closure construction and §4.1.4(a), final paragraph: ordered compactification of the target correspondence, proper-leg closure, and source-correspondence closure; the Cartesian restrictions are proved from scheme-theoretic image restriction.
